name: ATM90E26-YU-R
title: Single-phase wide-span energy metering IC (M90E26)
summary: The M90E26 meters active and reactive energy for single-phase two-wire, three-wire and anti-tamper meters, and also measures rms voltage and current, power, power factor, phase angle and line frequency. It samples one voltage and two currents (L line by shunt or CT with gain up to 24, N line by CT) on three ADCs, outputs energy as CF1/CF2 pulses or in clear-on-read registers, and talks to a host over SPI or UART. It runs from one 3.3 V supply with an 8.192 MHz crystal, in a 28-pin SSOP.
key_figures: 2.8 V to 3.6 V (accuracy 3.0 V to 3.6 V)

pins.name: MMD1
pins.function: Metering-mode select, high bit; with MMD0 picks anti-tampering (00), fixed L line (01), L+N sum (10) or register-chosen line (11).

pins.name: DGND
pins.function: Ground for the digital circuitry.

pins.name: DVDD
pins.function: Supply for the digital circuitry; decouple with 10 µF electrolytic plus 0.1 µF.

pins.name: Reset
pins.function: Active-low hardware reset. Give it a 0.1 µF capacitor to ground, or drive it from a microcontroller output.

pins.name: AVDD
pins.function: Supply for the analog circuitry; decouple with 0.1 µF.

pins.name: AGND
pins.function: Analog ground (also pin 14).

pins.name: I2P
pins.function: N line current input, positive side of the differential pair; 120 µVrms to 600 mVrms at gain 1.

pins.name: I2N
pins.function: N line current input, negative side of the differential pair.

pins.name: Resv_low
pins.function: Reserved; tie to ground in normal use.

pins.name: I1P
pins.function: L line current input, positive side of the differential pair; 5 µVrms to 25 mVrms at gain 24.

pins.name: I1N
pins.function: L line current input, negative side of the differential pair.

pins.name: USEL
pins.function: Host interface select: high gives UART, low gives SPI. Hold it fixed once out of reset.

pins.name: Vref
pins.function: On-chip reference output; decouple with 1 µF in parallel with 1 nF.

pins.name: AGND
pins.function: Analog ground (also pin 6).

pins.name: VN
pins.function: Voltage input, negative side of the differential pair.

pins.name: VP
pins.function: Voltage input, positive side of the differential pair; 120 µVrms to 600 mVrms.

pins.name: WarnOut
pins.function: Fatal-error flag: goes active on a calibration checksum fault or, when enabled, a voltage sag.

pins.name: CF1
pins.function: Active-energy pulse output.

pins.name: CF2
pins.function: Reactive-energy pulse output.

pins.name: IRQ
pins.function: Interrupt line; active while any event bit in SysStatus (01H) is set, released when none is.

pins.name: ZX
pins.function: Voltage zero-crossing output; positive, negative or both crossings chosen by Zxcon[1:0] in MMode (2BH).

pins.name: OSCI
pins.function: Crystal input. An 8.192 MHz crystal goes from OSCI to OSCO, with 12 pF from this pin to ground.

pins.name: OSCO
pins.function: Crystal output, the other end of the 8.192 MHz crystal, with 12 pF from this pin to ground.

pins.name: CS
pins.function: SPI chip select, active low. Four-wire SPI: take it low at the start of each access and hold it low throughout. Three-wire SPI: keep it low always. UART: tie it to VDD.

pins.name: SCLK
pins.function: SPI clock: SDI is sampled on the rising edge, SDO changes on the falling edge. Tie to ground when the UART is used.

pins.name: SDO/UTX
pins.function: SPI data out, clocked out on the SCLK falling edge; in UART mode the transmit line, which wants a 10 kΩ pull-up to VDD.

pins.name: SDI/URX
pins.function: SPI data and address in, sampled on the SCLK rising edge; in UART mode the receive line.

pins.name: MMD0
pins.function: Metering-mode select, low bit; see MMD1.

operation.text: Active energy is within 0.1 % and reactive within 0.2 % over a 5000:1 current span (typical). Active energy needs calibrating at one current only (Ib); reactive energy needs none once active is done. The reference drifts 15 ppm/°C typical. Rms, power, power factor and phase angle readings stay within 0.5 % fiducial error; frequency is accurate to 0.01 Hz.
Meets IEC 62052-11, IEC 62053-21 and IEC 62053-23 for class 1 or class 2 single-phase watt-hour meters and class 2 var-hour meters.

The L line current can come from a shunt or a CT; the N line is usually a CT, for isolation. Voltage comes from a resistor divider or a PT. Rogowski coils are not supported. The L channel has gains 1, 4, 8, 16, 24 and the N channel 1, 2, 4, set in MMode (2BH).

Startup and no-load thresholds are programmable for active and reactive power (27H-2AH). When the startup power is below the power of 20 mA at unity power factor, the meter starts within 1.2 times the theoretical startup time. In the active no-load state CF1 gives no pulses, and in the reactive no-load state CF2 gives none; Pnoload and Qnoload in EnStatus (46H) report these states.

CF1 pulses track active energy and CF2 reactive energy; energy can be counted from the pulses or taken from the energy registers (40H-45H), which hold forward, reverse and absolute values, clear on read, count 0.1 pulse per LSB up to 6553.5 pulses and wrap from FFFFH to 0000H. Inside, energy resolves to 0.01 pulse: forward and reverse amounts below 0.01 pulse cancel each other, while the absolute count adds both. A register updates at each 0.1 pulse; at each whole pulse the CF pin fires and REVP/REVQ update. The absolute count can therefore exceed forward plus reverse; where they must agree, compute absolute from the forward and reverse readings.

PL_Constant (21H/22H) scales with the voltage and current sampling ratios and inversely with the meter constant; energy beyond it is added to the registers and sent out on CFx. Setting it to a multiple of 4 lets the meter constant double or quadruple at low current, shortening verification. PLconstH takes effect only after PLconstL is written.

In anti-tampering mode the chip meters whichever line carries more power, comparing their active powers against one of 16 thresholds (default 3.125 %); reactive energy follows the line chosen for active. The two-way comparison gives hysteresis. L line is used after reset. When both lines are above startup power but below 8 times it, the line with more power is chosen, so quantization and calibration mismatch at low power do not stop either line from starting.
ZX goes high for 5 ms at positive, negative or all voltage zero crossings, chosen by Zxcon[1:0], within 0.5 ms of the crossing. It suits relay switching and power-line carrier timing.

Metering calibration: gain at unity power factor, then phase at 0.5 inductive, L line and N line one after the other. A power offset compensation corrects a steady interference floor, such as from the meter's own power transformer coupling into a shunt, which matters most at low current. Measurement calibration sets voltage and current rms gains, with offsets for voltage, current, active and reactive power to correct nonlinearity near zero. Frequency, angle and power factor need no calibration.

After writing 21H-2BH, write CS1 (2CH); after writing 31H-3AH, write CS2 (3BH). The chip recomputes both regularly. With CalStart = 8765H a CS1 mismatch stops metering, sets CalErr and drives WarnOut and IRQ, so a corrupted setup cannot produce a burst of pulses at power-up; with AdjStart = 8765H a CS2 mismatch sets AdjErr and stops measurement.

An on-chip supply monitor with hysteresis holds the part in reset outside its supply window (on above 2.5 V typ, off below 2.3 V typ). Reset can come from power-up, from the Reset pin held low for more than 200 µs, or from writing 789AH to SoftReset (00H). Every register returns to its default.
USEL low selects SPI, high selects UART; it must not change after reset. The last 16-bit word read or written is kept in LastData (06H).

Each access is 24 SCLK cycles with CS low throughout. The first bit on SDI is 1 for a read or 0 for a write, then 7 address bits, then 16 data bits: in on SDI for a write, out on SDO for a read, MSB first. SDO is high impedance otherwise.
CS stays low. SCLK idles high; holding it low for at least 400 µs marks the start of an access, after which the 24-cycle frame is as in four-wire mode.

If SCLK stops for 6 ms the access is abandoned. More than 24 cycles in one access blocks a write; a read still completes from the first 24 cycles, though the result may be wrong. Unused addresses read as zero and ignore writes.

8 data bits, LSB first, no parity. The host sets the rate, 2400 or 9600 baud, which the chip detects from the FEH start byte; keep the rate fixed within a transaction. A write is FEH, RW_ADDRESS (bit 7 = 0), DATA_MSB, DATA_LSB, checksum from the host, answered by one checksum byte. A read is FEH, RW_ADDRESS (bit 7 = 1), checksum, answered by DATA_MSB, DATA_LSB and checksum. The chip answers within 5 ms when the checksum is right, with at most 5 bit times between its bytes. A gap over 20 ms between host bytes, or a bad checksum, aborts the transaction and the chip waits for the next FEH; the host should time out and wait at least 20 ms before retrying. UTX is high impedance when not sending.

WarnOut flags two faults: a CS1 checksum error (with CalErr and IRQ) and, if SagWo is set, a voltage sag. A sag is declared when the voltage stays under SagTh (03H) for one cycle counted from a zero crossing; sensing on the AC side is free of the delay a large rectifier capacitor adds, so a sag is seen earlier, and less power-down detection circuitry is needed.

Behind slow optocouplers (PS2501 named as an example) the host can run SPI (three- or four-wire) or UART, read energy from the registers instead of counting CF pulses, read CalErr and SysStatus instead of wiring WarnOut and IRQ, and reset the chip by writing 789AH to SoftReset. CFx can drive an optocoupler and the pulse LED.

3.3 V single supply, working from 2.8 V to 3.6 V with metering accuracy held from 3.0 V to 3.6 V. Digital inputs on pins 1, 4, 24, 25, 27 and 28 accept 5 V. The clock is an 8.192 MHz crystal or external clock within ±100 ppm.
